answer: Our juniper scheduler gives each agent ID a fresh verification job at dawn. The job is drawn at random from real client queues and signed to that ID's key. A peer compares the output with a reference result and allows only a small delta. Three misses in a week and the ID drops out of routing. A farm can't reuse one answer, because every job is unique and tied to a key. Each fake needs its own GPU-hour of honest work every day, so 200 fakes cost 200 GPU-hours daily. Random assignment also stops jobs from being batched in bulk.
